# Running the lessons locally {#sec-setup}

Lessons that run in the browser need no setup. For lessons that fit models
with PyMC and Bambi, you need Python on your own computer. There are two ways
to get it.

## Option 1: the whole book with pixi (recommended)

[pixi](https://pixi.prefix.dev) installs Python and every package the book
uses into a folder inside the project, without touching the rest of your
system.

1. Install pixi by following the
   [installation instructions](https://pixi.prefix.dev/latest/installation/)
   for your operating system.
2. Download the book's code, either with git:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/jobindjohn/bayesian-biomechanics.git
   cd bayesian-biomechanics
   ```

   or by downloading and unzipping the
   [ZIP archive](https://github.com/jobindjohn/bayesian-biomechanics/archive/refs/heads/main.zip).
3. Open a lesson. The first run downloads and installs everything, which can
   take a few minutes:

   ```bash
   pixi run lesson 02-first-regression/first_regression.py
   ```

The lesson opens in your web browser.

### Re-fitting the models

Lessons load pre-computed results when they exist, so they open quickly. To
fit the models again from scratch and overwrite the saved results:

```bash
pixi run refit 02-first-regression/first_regression.py
```

## Option 2: a single notebook

Every notebook lists the packages it needs at the top of the file, so you can
run one on its own. Download it with the button on the lesson's page, then
use either of:

- **uv** ([installation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)):

  ```bash
  uvx marimo edit --sandbox first_regression.py
  ```

- **pixi**:

  ```bash
  pixi exec marimo edit first_regression.py
  ```
